_meta.field: true_starts = 1-based physical page indices at which a distinct piece begins; [] means the file is not a compilation and nothing should be emitted
_meta.sampling: uniform random over `doc_type: issue_compilation` sidecars, one file per domain, restricted to domains NOT touched during development of the running-head rules or of toc_solver.py (see hold_out_of). File size > 400kB. seed 1234.
_meta.method: every page of every file was read (first 3-5 lines plus the last 2 lines, extracted with PyMuPDF) and openings were marked before any solver output was inspected. Openings were identified by display title + byline + absence of a running head, corroborated by the folio stream.
_meta.labeller: LLM (Claude), single pass. NOT human-adjudicated -- scoring an LLM detector against this measures agreement with one LLM reading, not correctness. The project assumes a ~2-3% gold noise floor.
judgment_calls: a panel piece whose participant-bio page precedes its annotated transcript counts as ONE piece, starting at the bio page (digitalcommons.wcl.american.edu p52, p80)
an editor's note / foreword counts as a piece (www.nyulawreview.org p3)
front matter (cover, masthead, contents, faculty roster, colophon) is never an opening
a single article that happens to carry its own table of contents is not a compilation: true_starts is [] and the correct behaviour is to abstain
known_gaps: www.aipla.org/2022-01-01-form-20-f-2022-en.pdf was drawn by the sample and dropped unlabelled: it is an SEC Form 20-F, not law-review content
9 issues is a small held-out set; it bounds nothing tightly. It is enough to detect a splitter that cuts mid-article, not enough to certify 99.9% precision

notes: one article, 'From Fingerprints to Opioids', printed pp. 375-402. Carries its own TABLE OF CONTENTS on p1 whose entries (I. INTRODUCTION ... 375) are section headings, not articles. This is the trap that an unguarded TOC parser turns into eight corrupt children.
one article, Cavallaro & Saldanha, printed pp. 153-182. No contents listing.
one piece by Byron F. Egan plus Appendices A and B. Carries its own TABLE OF CONTENTS on p1. APPENDIX A (p23) and APPENDIX B (p38) are parts of the piece, not separate works.
one article, 'Chevron and Originalism', printed pp. 1281-1327. Word production slug on every page.
1926 Indiana State Bar Association proceedings: one continuous transcript with a list of applicants appended at p140. No contents listing, no article structure.

Connecticut Insurance Law Journal 31.2. Front matter pp1-10 (cover, masthead, faculty roster p5-7, contents p9). Offset is a clean +74 throughout. Word production slug head; the slug prints on the opening page too.
American University Labor & Employment Law Forum 1:3. Contents on p8. p56 and p82 are 'ANNOTATED TRANSCRIPT' second title pages inside the panel pieces that open at p52 and p80 -- see judgment_calls.
Chapman Law Review 28:1. Front matter pp1-11 (editor's note pp9-11), colophon p252. Offset -11. Verso head is the journal name, recto head is the short title.

NYU Law Review 'Women & Law' joint publication, 15 pieces. NO contents listing anywhere in the file, so a TOC-driven solver must abstain here; the pieces are nonetheless real and this file is what abstention costs. The folio stream also drifts (unnumbered divider pages), so a single global offset does not hold across the whole file.
